name: one-simdgroup-through-ten-shuffle-shapes
rationale:
One 32-lane simdgroup, one invocation per lane, reading itself through ten shuffle shapes at once: simd_shuffle_and_fill_up and _down on uint, float, float3 and half4, plus the plain simd_shuffle_up on float3 and simd_shuffle_down on uint2 and half3. Those ten AIR symbols are 178 corpus sources between them and the largest uncovered block left; every corpus host buries them in a loop or a function-constant-gated region, so a fixture is the only way to reach them.

Every lane's datum is its own index plus one and its fill datum is a hundred plus its index, so the 32 data values and the 32 fill values are disjoint and each is distinct: the lane a result came from, and whether it came from the data or the fill operand, are both readable straight off the answer. The four deltas differ (3, 5, 2, 4, 1, 9) so no two of the fill shapes can be confused with each other, and delta 9 on the float shape puts more than a quarter of the group on the fill side. All the values are small integers held exactly by float and by half -- the largest half is 134 and the largest float is 524 -- and the vector lanes scale by two and four, so the whole comparison is exact without depending on any rounding.

The three plain shuffles have no fill operand, and Metal leaves a lane whose source index leaves the simdgroup undefined. Exactly those lanes -- below 6 for the up shuffle, at or above 25 and 27 for the two down shuffles -- have their slots overwritten with zero after the unconditional store, so the case compares only the lanes Metal defines while still making the call on all 32.

name: constant-buffer-float4-to-mrt3-highest
rationale: The loop-free fragment converts the exact finite float4 color in the 32-byte constant buffer to half4 and structurally inserts that same value into all three return members; selecting attachment two verifies the complete three-target aggregate mapping.

name: alias-a-tile-cell-onto-render-target-0
rationale: A tile kernel whose EXPLICIT imageblock carries `air.alias_implicit_imageblock`, so its cell is not tile-local scratch but the render targets themselves. Compared in colour attachment 0. Every lane written is a function of lanes READ from the cell, so a cell that started as undefined scratch answers differently at every texel, and the comparison is made in the attachment, so a cell that never reached one answers differently again. The AIR is the corpus's widest aliased layout byte for byte -- {half4, half4, half}, 24 bytes -- and 30 of the 14579 corpus sources carry the marker in four layouts of which this is one. Lane 0 comes from colour, lane 1 from aux and lane 2 from depth, so answering any plane from the wrong attachment moves the answer. Initial texels are colour = (x, y, x + 16y, 1), aux = (x + 300, y + 300, 600 + x + 16y, 7) and depth = 100 + x + 16y; all 256 are distinct and every result is an integer below 2048, exact in binary16, so no lane depends on rounding, on fast math, or on association. Derived closed form: (x + 1, y + 302, 103 + x + 16y, 2). Metal reproduced it exactly at all 256 texels.

name: alias-a-tile-cell-onto-render-target-1
rationale: The sibling of alias-a-tile-cell-onto-render-target-0 compared in colour attachment 1, which is the SECOND member of the aliased imageblock struct. A single-output case cannot show that a write to member 1 reached attachment 1 rather than attachment 0, so each attachment gets its own case over the same dispatch. Lane 0 comes from aux, lane 1 from colour and lane 2 from depth, so this plane also fails under any attachment permutation. Derived closed form: (2x + 600, y + 4, 300 + 3x + 48y, 12), every lane an integer below 2048 and therefore exact in binary16. Metal reproduced it exactly at all 256 texels.

name: alias-a-tile-cell-onto-render-target-2
rationale: The sibling of alias-a-tile-cell-onto-render-target-0 compared in colour attachment 2, the THIRD member of the aliased struct. This is the case that settles what the member's name does not: the member is typed `half` and the corpus calls it `depth`, and it is still COLOUR attachment 2 -- an r16_float render target -- because it is declared third. Nothing about the mapping keys on a member name. Its value is the sum of the third lane of all three planes, 700 + 3x + 48y, an integer below 2048 and so exact in binary16 whichever way the two additions are associated. Metal reproduced it exactly at all 256 texels.

name: nan-model-float-to-half-narrowing-and-half-arithmetic-under-fast-math
rationale: nan_narrow_fast (nan_narrow's program under the default fast math, where the half +, *, air.fma, and fneg carry fast) at nan_narrow's lanes: which half Metal's narrowing of a float NaN answers, and which NaN its flagged half arithmetic answers (DESIGN D293): lane i reads a float a and halves ha, hb, hc, and writes half(a), float(half(a)), ha + hb | ha * hb << 16, and fma(ha, hb, hc) | -ha << 16. Lanes: every float NaN and the narrowing's range and rounding edges; each half NaN (quiet and signaling of either sign, payloads 0, 1, 2, 0xaa, 0x155, 0x1fe, 0x1ff) as ha then hb against 1.0, two distinct NaNs, a NaN addend, NaN-generating operands, and controls. Every operand is loaded from a buffer, so nothing folds but what the AIR shows. NaN operands: quiet and signaling of either sign with payloads 0, 1, 2, 0x1000, 0x155555, 0x2aaaaa, 0x3ffffe, 0x3fffff. The output is pre-filled with 0xAB.

name: read-a-scalar-and-a-vector-through-one-byte-view
rationale: A device pointer parked in a struct field and read back by an OUT-OF-LINE helper, which is the shape that leaves the pointer a Private byte placeholder while the helper is emitted: the store that gave it an address is in the caller, so the byte-view loads have to be deferred and repaired after inlining. The helper reads a packed_float3 at +0 and a lone float at +12 from the same dynamic base, and both reach the emitter as scalar float loads through a uchar pointer. Before the fix this module could not be translated at all -- emit_scalar_slots_to_wider_load assembled a wider VECTOR result from narrow slots but declined a scalar one, and the load reported 'cannot reinterpret load of byte pointer to Float without a logical-pointer bitcast'; ten corpus sources failed on that asymmetry. The eight records hold distinct exactly-representable floats, so an assembly that reads the wrong bytes, or that reads Private scratch instead of the bound buffer, cannot reproduce the output.

name: visible-table-clear-slots-two-through-twelve-dual-output
rationale: One invocation calls visible-function-table slots 2 through 12 and receives exact float4 zero from all eleven linked _uber_clear bodies. A fourteen-word size table and eight explicit argument-info records keep every selector and offset in bounds; register 2 is selected. This entry swizzles it to float4(0,0,0,1), writes both required poisoned output textures, and captures binding zero byte-exactly.

name: visible-table-clear-slots-two-through-eight-rgb-lane-output
rationale: One invocation calls visible-function-table slots 2 through 8 and receives exact float4 zero from all seven linked _uber_clear bodies. A ten-word size table and eight explicit argument-info records keep every selector and offset in bounds; register 2 is selected. This entry splats the selected R, G, and B lanes into the complete poisoned 3x1 primary footprint byte-exactly.

name: one-simdgroup-through-ten-matrix-8x8-shapes
rationale:
One 32-lane simdgroup driving ten `air.simdgroup_matrix_8x8_*` families: the load and store at both float and half, the diagonal init at both, and the multiply-accumulate at all four precision mixes the corpus uses. Every matrix holds small integers, so every product and sum is exact at half as well as float and no rounding decision is involved.

The first accumulate is the only non-trivial matmul and it is deliberately asymmetric: B is a cyclic column shift, so `A*B + C` rotates A's columns before adding C and neither a transposed load nor a swapped `A*B` / `B*A` reproduces it. Row 0 of the result is 107, 101, 103 ... 113 while column 0 is 107, 123, 139 ... 219. The other four accumulate against a diagonal, which isolates the precision mix from the matmul: `Ah*I + C` and `A*I + C` must answer the SAME 64 words even though one takes its left operand at half and the other at float, so a mix that widens the wrong operand shows up as a disagreement between two slots of one output.

The results are stored to device scratch and read back through the compared buffer, so the store lowering is verified rather than merely reached. The 321st word is left at the 0xABABABAB fill and read back as an overrun guard.

name: linked-single-unit-average-simd-tmp-output
rationale: Every source, destination, kernel, stride, dilation, threadgroup cube, and group-count extent is exactly one with zero offsets. The required multi-destination constants select one float source and one active float destination; the explicit temporary buffer is one float, so this pooling variant executes a bounded unit window and exposes its exact written result.

name: seventeen-integer-intrinsics-at-their-edges
rationale: Seventeen integer intrinsics over a 12-value edge grid rotated so every value meets every other: clz and ctz at zero, where SPIR-V's FindUMsb/FindILsb answer -1 and Metal answers the width; abs at INT_MIN, which has no positive image; reverse_bits and rotate, which no corpus host makes value-observable; mul_hi and mad_sat at the products that overflow 32 bits; extract_bits signed and unsigned including the offset+count==32 boundary; insert_bits at that same boundary; rhadd, add_sat and sub_sat at their carries; and clamp with its bounds ordered. Offsets and counts are masked so no bitfield call leaves its defined domain, and every operand is read from a buffer so nothing folds to a constant.

name: discard-where-fmod-leaves-the-cosine-positive
no_effect: The cosine is positive, so the fragment discards and the render target keeps its authored bytes.
rationale: The entry has no resources at all, so the generated companion fixes every input: the scalar varyings dashFactor and t are both 0.25. air.fast_fmod.f32(0.25, 2*pi) must be 0.25 because the quotient truncates to zero, and air.fast_cos.f32(0.25*0.25 - 0.125) is then cos(-0.0625), which is positive by a margin of a whole quadrant, so the fragment discards and the render target keeps its authored bytes. The case pins the discard: an fmod that returns the dividend unreduced, or a cosine whose sign is wrong here, writes the colour instead.

name: negative-cosine-keeps-the-fragment-and-writes-the-scaled-color
rationale: Reaching variant of this entry's discarding case (TODO 6.2, WP-RVC), whose passthrough defaults (every scalar varying 0.25) make the fragment discard. The entry has no resources, so the varyings are its only inputs, and the case authors their values (varying_values, DESIGN D431): the passthrough vertex writes each at all three vertices, so the single fragment of the 1x1 rgba16_float target receives exactly that value. t = 1.0 passes t <= 1 (ule, equal) and dashFactor = 4.0 passes > 0, so the fragment evaluates the cosine: fast_fmod(4.0, 6.2831855) is 4.0 (the dividend is below the divisor, so the quotient truncates to zero and the remainder is the dividend), times 0.5 is 2.0, and t * dashFactor - 2.0 = 2.0, whose cosine is -0.416, negative by a margin far beyond fast_cos's error, so the fragment does not discard and writes half4(0.5, 1.0, 0.25, 1.0) * 0.75 = (0.375, 0.75, 0.1875, 0.75). Every value is a small multiple of a power of two, exact in float and in half, so each fptrunc and each half product is exact; the render target's authored 0xab bytes differ from every written half. The function has no loop.

name: t-above-one-skips-the-dash-test-and-writes-the-scaled-color
rationale: Reaching variant of this entry's discarding case (TODO 6.2, WP-RVC), whose passthrough defaults (every scalar varying 0.25) make the fragment discard. The entry has no resources, so the varyings are its only inputs, and the case authors their values (varying_values, DESIGN D431): the passthrough vertex writes each at all three vertices, so the single fragment of the 1x1 rgba16_float target receives exactly that value. t = 2.0 fails the first test (t <= 1), so the select is false whatever dashFactor holds (left at the passthrough's default 0.25) and the fragment skips the cosine and writes half4(0.75, 0.25, 1.0, 1.0) * 0.5 = (0.375, 0.125, 0.5, 0.5). Every value is a small multiple of a power of two, exact in float and in half, so each fptrunc and each half product is exact; the render target's authored 0xab bytes differ from every written half. The function has no loop.

name: vertex-float2-position-with-buffer-depth
rationale: Three authored float2 positions form a full-coverage triangle; constant buffer slot 1 supplies finite clip-space depth 0.25, and the typed position observer captures the structural expansion to (x, y, depth, 1).

name: half-math-functions-at-the-lanes-devices-answer-otherwise-under-fast-math
rationale: Each of 32 threads writes 8 words, two halves each, for its half pair (a, b), compiled with the default fast math: (sin a, cos a), (tan a, asin a), (acos a, atan a), (atan2(a, b), fmod(a, b)), (sqrt a, rsqrt a), (pow(a, b), powr(a, b)), (sinpi a, cospi a), and (tanpi a, b). Operands, 32 (a, b) half pairs: both zeros (the signs of sin, tan, asin, and atan of a zero); fmod(x, +-inf) at x = +0, -0, 1, -1, 2.5, -2.5 (Metal answers x); fmod(1.5, -0.75) (an exact zero); sqrt(65504) (255.875 correctly rounded); atan2, pow, and powr at (3, 7), (-0.300048828125, 0.7001953125), and (7, 3); then 0.5, -0.5, 0.25, 100, -100, 0.999, 2, the smallest normal and 2^-13, the smallest denormals of both signs, 1000, +-3.14, 0.75, 60000, +-6.5, and 1 against various b, and fmod(1, 0). Question (WP-TRN, DESIGN D297): Metal's half answers at the lanes where a device, or the translation's float routines rounded to half, were seen to differ, so the venues' answers can be read against Metal's afresh.

name: visible-table-clear-slots-two-through-thirty-threadgroup-primary
rationale: One invocation calls visible-function-table slots 2 through 30 and receives exact float4 zero from all twenty-nine linked _uber_clear bodies. A thirty-two-word size table and eight explicit argument-info records keep every selector and offset in bounds; register 2 is selected. The single-invocation threadgroup executes both barriers over internal static storage and writes the linked result to the poisoned primary texel byte-exactly.

name: linked-single-lane-mx-dequantize
no_effect: The linked destination callback is a no-op by design, so the destination element keeps its authored bytes while the dequantization path runs.
rationale: One invocation reads exactly four packed quantized bytes and one shared scale byte from the two authored device-array inputs. The exact linked primary float4 destination is the retained no-op callback; the sole poisoned destination element therefore remains byte-exact and proves the linked callback contract while the dequantization path executes.

name: sixteen-lanes-dequantize-through-the-public-linked-destination
rationale: Reaching variant of the single-lane case of this entry (TODO 6.2, WP-RVC), whose linked destination callback was the retained postfixPrimary_4xf, which writes nothing. This case links the public module validation/fixtures/public/linked/mps_postfix_primary_4xf_to_last_buffer (owned MSL, DESIGN D431 item 2): it stores the float4 at elements coordinate.x to coordinate.x + 3 of the kernel's buffer table's last array (constant 122 = 3 gives the kernel three arrays, and the callback the count 3), so each dequantized value reaches the destination. Sixteen threads (one threadgroup) each read 4 packed bytes of FP8 E5M2 bytes at 4 * gid.x from array 0 and one scale byte at (4 gid.x) >> 5 from array 1 (E8M0 scale bytes 0x7d (0.25), 0x70 (3.05176e-05), one per 32 elements); thread gid.x writes elements 4 gid.x to 4 gid.x + 3 of array 2 (256 bytes, poisoned 0xab before), so every thread's four words are observed and none overlaps another's. The codes spread over the format's nonzero finite encodings (no zero of either sign, whose sign the kernels' fast math leaves unspecified, and no NaN or infinity); every decoded value times its scale is a normal float, exact, 48 distinct words. Straight-line code: no loop.

name: take-a-two-channel-vector-median-over-a-clamped-neighbourhood
rationale:
medianFilterRef is a two-channel vector median: it stages the 3x3 neighbourhood of its thread into a private array, then for each of the nine candidates sums the absolute difference to all nine and keeps the candidate whose total is smallest, per channel independently. The running minimum is `air.fmin.v2f16` and the neighbourhood coordinate is `air.clamp.s.v2i16` against zero and the texture extent the kernel reads back with `air.get_width_texture_2d` and `air.get_height_texture_2d`.

The clamp is the reason the grid is the whole four-by-four texture rather than its interior. Twelve of the sixteen threads sit on a border, where the neighbourhood offset makes a coordinate -1 or 4. That clamp is signed: -1 has to land on 0. Read as unsigned, -1 is 65535 and would clamp to the far edge instead, so every border thread would take its neighbourhood from the opposite side of the image and produce a different median. Nothing else in the kernel distinguishes the two readings.

Every texel is an integer between 0 and 64, so each of the nine absolute differences is an integer below 65 and each total is an integer below 577 -- exact in binary16 at every partial sum, and therefore the same total whichever association the fast-math flags choose for the nine-term accumulation. The values were drawn until no lane of any thread has a tie for the minimum, so the `<` that breaks ties by iteration order never has to: the winner is the unique minimum and does not depend on the order the nine candidates are visited. The two channels carry unrelated values, so a lowering that collapsed the per-lane selects into one would pick the same candidate for both and disagree at most threads.

The kernel writes `(median.r, median.g, median.g, median.g)`, so the expectation repeats the green median three times -- the shuffle that does it is the last instruction before the store, and swapping its lanes would show up in the blue and alpha channels.

name: visible-table-clear-slots-two-through-twenty-six-simd-primary
rationale: One invocation calls visible-function-table slots 2 through 26 and receives exact float4 zero from all twenty-five linked _uber_clear bodies. A twenty-eight-word size table and eight explicit argument-info records keep every selector and offset in bounds; register 2 is selected. The entry writes that result to the poisoned primary texel before subgroup aggregation, and binding zero is captured byte-exactly.

name: visible-table-clear-slots-two-through-ten
rationale: One invocation calls visible-function-table slots 2 through 10 and receives exact float4 zero from all nine linked _uber_clear bodies. A twelve-word size table and eight explicit argument-info records keep every selector and offset in bounds; the final selector reads register 2 and writes exact zero to the poisoned primary texel.

name: fragment-varying-float-to-half
rationale: The fragment entry truncates its perspective center scalar float varying to half and writes color location zero; the shared generated fullscreen vertex stage supplies the varying and the selected R16Float pixel captures the conversion byte-exactly.

name: gather-mm-rhs-nt-float-k40-two-experts
rationale: Reaching variant of the zero-shape case of this entry (TODO 6.2, WP-RVC), whose zero extents stop the kernel before its arithmetic. One threadgroup of 64 lanes (2 simdgroups) runs the single 16x64 output tile: B = 1, M = 16, N = 64, K = 40 (gemm_k_iterations_aligned = 2, remainder 8), no dimension declared aligned (user constant 0): the remainder and both whole blocks go through the guarded loader; constant 122 binds a two-entry table. The indices select expert 0 for rows below 8 and expert 1 for the rest, so the kernel walks two row segments, each a full tile multiply over its expert (experts_stride_b = N*K = 2560), writing only its own rows. B[e][n][k] (ldb = 40): expert 0 holds q(n, k) = (11n + 3k + floor(3nk/5)) mod 16, nonlinear in n, so the 64 column sums differ, and expert 1 holds q/2. A[m][k] (lda = 40): rows of segment 0 hold a = 1, 2, 3, 4, 5 repeating along k, rows of segment 1 hold 2a, so every row of the result is the same (2a . q/2 = a . q): the linked destination callback, which writes table entry 1 at the column coordinate only, stores one value per column from every row, the same value, so the 64 words observed (256 bytes) do not depend on write order, and a row given the other segment's expert would write another. Every input is a multiple of 0.5 at most 15, exact in float; every product is a multiple of 0.5 at most 75 and every sum of 40 at most 3000, below 2^12: exact in float in any order or contraction. Every loop is finite by these inputs: the row-segment scan stops at M = 16, the K loop runs gemm_k_iterations_aligned = 2 times, the segment loop ends after the two segments, and the element loops have constant trip counts.

name: gather-mm-rhs-nt-float-zero-shape
no_effect: The authored parameters give the work an empty extent, so the entry returns before any write reaches the selected output.
rationale: The nt float counterpart of the committed mps_gather_mm_rhs_nn_half case (DESIGN D272): mps_gather_mm_rhs_nt_float with the same function constants, resources, one-thread dispatch, and linked visible function (postfixPrimary_f). Its zero extents keep every loop bound finite, so the case observes the four-byte destination allocation; the kernel links translation units each with its own static initializer and no llvm.global_ctors list, and calls matmul2d, so its translation exercises the unordered-initializer rule (D272.4) and the matmul2d lowering (D272.3). Replaced (DESIGN D296): the linked destination callback writes table entry 1, so the case binds a two-entry table (MPSNDArrayRefSize 1 source, 1 destination) whose destination element carries the source element's fill.

name: ldexp-past-what-a-scale-factor-can-hold
rationale:
Eight ldexp calls whose exponents are deliberately larger than float32 can hold on their own. ldexp scales the exponent field, so the only thing that has to be representable is the RESULT; building it as x * exp2(float(n)) instead materializes the scale factor as its own float32, and that factor overflows above 127 and flushes to zero below -126 even when the product is an ordinary number.

The first three arguments are exactly that hole. 1e-30 scaled by 2^200 is 1.6069381e30 and 1e30 scaled by 2^-200 is 6.2230154e-31 -- both perfectly ordinary float32 numbers whose scale factors are not; the third takes the smallest normal, 2^-126, all the way to the largest, 2^127, a swing of 253 binades in one call, which is the widest this type can express at all. Each of the three is exact: ldexp only moves the exponent, so the result carries the mantissa of the argument unchanged, and all three were derived in float64 and rounded once.

The remaining five hold the ordinary behaviour still. 3.5 by 2^4 is 56; 1 by 2^127 and 1 by 2^-126 are the two endpoints of the normal range, reached exactly; -2.5 by 2^100 carries the sign; and 123456.75 by 2^-17 is a full 24-bit mantissa surviving a shift into a fraction. Twenty-four arguments across this range were probed, including zero, negative zero and the denormal flush below 2^-126 where Metal and this translator both answer exactly zero.

name: coverage-and-pixel-center-read-by-each-run-at-4x
rationale: A memory writer that reads [[sample_mask]] and [[position]] and no sample index, in a 1x1 pass without attachments at 4 samples, drawn by the generated full-screen triangle: as the coverage case, and word 18 ORs the position times 4, rounded: every run reads the pixel center (0.5, 0.5), 0x202. On MoltenVK, which runs a memory writer once per covered sample itself, it runs as written (D341 item 9); elsewhere it loops over its covered samples.

name: coverage-beside-a-sample-varying-at-2x
rationale: A memory writer that reads [[sample_mask]] and a [[sample_perspective]] float2 (the companion's uv = 2a) and no sample index, in a 1x1 pass without attachments at 2 samples, drawn by the generated full-screen triangle: word round(8 uv.x) ORs the coverage, round(8 uv.y) in bits 8-15 and bit 16, word 16 + that slot counts the run. Metal's 2-sample positions (0.75, 0.75) and (0.25, 0.25) read uv (0.75, 0.25) and (0.25, 0.75). On MoltenVK, which runs a memory writer once per covered sample itself, it runs as written (D341 item 9); elsewhere it loops over its covered samples.

name: coverage-beside-a-sample-varying-at-4x
rationale: The same at 4 samples, at Metal's 4-sample positions, where Apple splits the pixel. On MoltenVK, which runs a memory writer once per covered sample itself, it runs as written (D341 item 9); elsewhere it loops over its covered samples.

name: coverage-read-by-each-run-of-a-memory-writer-at-2x
rationale: A fragment function that reads [[sample_mask]] and writes memory, in a 1x1 pass without attachments at 2 samples, drawn by the generated full-screen triangle: Metal runs it once per covered sample, each run reading the pixel's coverage (D341). Word 0 ORs the coverages read, word 1 counts the runs, word 2 + c counts the runs that read c: 0x3, 2, and 2 runs of 0x3. On MoltenVK, which runs a memory writer once per covered sample itself, it runs as written (D341 item 9); elsewhere it loops over its covered samples.

name: coverage-read-by-each-run-of-a-memory-writer-at-4x
rationale: The same at 4 samples, where Apple's rasterizer splits the clipped triangle's pixel (D341 item 6): two runs read 0x3 and two 0xc. On MoltenVK, which runs a memory writer once per covered sample itself, it runs as written (D341 item 9); elsewhere it loops over its covered samples.

name: coverage-read-by-each-sample-run-at-2x
rationale: A memory writer that reads [[sample_mask]] and [[sample_id]] and no [[position]], in a 1x1 pass without attachments at 2 samples, drawn by the generated full-screen triangle: word s ORs the run's coverage | 0x100, word 8 + s counts the runs: 0x103 and 1 for samples 0 and 1. On MoltenVK, which runs a memory writer once per covered sample itself, it runs as written (D341 item 9); elsewhere it loops over its covered samples.

name: coverage-read-by-each-sample-run-at-4x
rationale: The same at 4 samples, where Apple splits the pixel: samples 0 and 1 read 0x3, samples 2 and 3 read 0xc, each run once. On MoltenVK, which runs a memory writer once per covered sample itself, it runs as written (D341 item 9); elsewhere it loops over its covered samples.

name: stage-in-elements-origin-and-size-of-an-executed-command-template
rationale: The compute template of executed commands whose stage-in region a kernel encodes (DESIGN D336), run as its own case: 8 threads in one threadgroup, stage input 0 a uint of stride 4 (element i = 0x5000 + 3 * i), and the oracle's region of the grid (origin 0, size 8 x 1 x 1). Thread t writes out[t] = (0x5000 + 3 * t, 0, 0x010108, t).

name: stage-in-of-a-dynamic-stride-layout-of-an-executed-command-template
rationale: The compute template of executed commands whose kernel buffers the host binds at attribute strides (DESIGN D327 item 5, D336), run as its own case: icb_stage_in_template under a stage-input layout of MTLBufferLayoutStrideDynamic, so the fetch reads the stride the data is bound with. 8 threads in one threadgroup, stage input 0 a uint whose data both executors bind with the stride form at stride 4 (element i = 0x5000 + 3 * i), and the oracle's region of the grid (origin 0, size 8 x 1 x 1). Thread t writes out[t] = (0x5000 + 3 * t, 0, 0x010108, t), as the fixed-stride template's case does.

name: linked-single-unit-reduce-multiple-passes-axes-min-propagate-NaN
rationale: One invocation reduces one float element along axis zero. Every four-lane reduction extent, per-thread count, per-threadgroup count, source and destination bound, broadcast extent, and NDArray size and stride is one, so all loops are bounded by the single authored element.

name: visible-table-clear-slots-two-through-seventeen-threadgroup-primary
rationale: One invocation calls visible-function-table slots 2 through 17 and receives exact float4 zero from all sixteen linked _uber_clear bodies. A nineteen-word size table and eight explicit argument-info records keep every selector and offset in bounds; register 2 is selected. The single-invocation threadgroup executes both barriers over internal static storage and writes the linked result to the poisoned primary texel byte-exactly.

name: residency-of-a-level-past-a-one-level-sparse-texture
rationale: D264.11's second item: a level outside a sparse texture under the sparse arm, measured on Metal: a read at lod 1 of a one-level sparse 2D texture, past its level count, at a mapped and an unmapped texel's coordinates, and samples at a level past the count, which Metal clamps into the texture. A sparse texture (D264) is made on Metal from a sparse heap of 16 KiB pages and mapped with MTLResourceStateCommandEncoder before the work, and on Vulkan as a sparse resident image bound with vkQueueBindSparse; only the mapped texels' authored bytes are uploaded. Each region is a whole number of tiles on every device that runs the case (an executor refuses a region that is not whole tiles of its device), so the mapped texels are the same wherever the case runs; each run prints its tiling. Texture 0 is 256x128 r32_float with texel (x, y) = 1000y + x + 1 (exact binary32) and its left 128x128 mapped (x 128..255 unmapped). name: sub-texel-quantum-of-a-linear-sample-across-a-width-that-is-not-a-power-of-two

The output is pre-filled with 0xAB, so an unwritten word shows; the AIR has no loop. Kind 0 is sparse_read(uint2(x, y), lod) of texture 0 (sampled, so a fetch at that level), 1 sparse_sample through a constexpr nearest clamp_to_zero normalized sampler at level(lodf), 2 the same through a linear one, 3 sparse_gather (component x) through the nearest one (level 0).
